analyzer_results.name: PhishGuard Local Heuristic+ML
analyzer_results.summary: Detected 14 indicator(s). Top signals: Credential or sensitive-info request; Reply-To domain mismatch; DMARC check did not pass (header claim). ML: phishing (100% phishing likelihood).

findings.title: Credential or sensitive-info request
findings.detail: Message appears to request login, verification, or sensitive information.

findings.title: Reply-To domain mismatch
findings.detail: From domain 'paypa1-secure.com' differs from Reply-To domain 'account-check.xyz'.

findings.title: DMARC check did not pass (header claim)
findings.detail: Authentication result header indicates dmarc=fail.
findings.reasoning: Header-reported authentication failures can indicate spoofing, but may also result from forwarding/misconfiguration; headers themselves are not independently verified here.
findings.recommended_action: Correlate with trusted mail infrastructure logs and other spoofing indicators before concluding.

findings.title: SPF check did not pass (header claim)
findings.detail: Authentication result header indicates spf=fail.
findings.reasoning: Header-reported authentication failures can indicate spoofing, but may also result from forwarding/misconfiguration; headers themselves are not independently verified here.
findings.recommended_action: Correlate with trusted mail infrastructure logs and other spoofing indicators before concluding.

findings.title: Possible display-name impersonation
findings.detail: Display name 'PayPal Security' references 'paypal' but sender domain is 'paypa1-secure.com'.
findings.reasoning: Brand names in display names can be abused to impersonate trusted organizations when the sender domain is unrelated.
findings.recommended_action: Verify the sender via official channels and inspect the actual From address/domain.

findings.title: Urgency/pressure language
findings.detail: Message uses urgency or fear-based pressure tactics.

findings.title: Link + credential request
findings.detail: Message combines links with credential/verification requests, a common phishing pattern.

findings.title: Suspicious TLD
findings.detail: Link uses higher-risk TLD '.top': https://paypa1-secure.com.login.verify-user.top/signin

findings.title: Complex/long domain
findings.detail: Link has an unusually complex host: paypa1-secure.com.login.verify-user.top

findings.title: Return-Path domain mismatch
findings.detail: Return-Path domain 'malicious-relay.top' differs from From domain 'paypa1-secure.com'.
findings.reasoning: Envelope sender and visible From domain differ; this can occur in legitimate forwarding/services but is also common in spoofing.
findings.recommended_action: Check alignment with SPF/DMARC context and sender legitimacy.

findings.title: Sensitive-action URL path/query
findings.detail: URL path/query contains sensitive action keywords: https://paypa1-secure.com.login.verify-user.top/signin
findings.reasoning: Legitimate services use such paths, but combined with other signals this can indicate credential harvesting.
findings.recommended_action: Confirm the destination is the official site before entering information.

findings.title: Generic greeting
findings.detail: Message uses a generic greeting instead of a personalized name.

findings.title: DKIM result is none (header claim)
findings.detail: Authentication result header indicates dkim=none; sender domain may lack alignment/configuration.
findings.reasoning: A 'none' result is weak evidence and common in some setups; it is not proof of phishing.
findings.recommended_action: Use as context only; prioritize stronger indicators.

findings.title: Authentication headers are unverified claims
findings.detail: SPF/DKIM/DMARC values are parsed from message headers (e.g. Authentication-Results/Received-SPF) and are not cryptographically or externally verified by this tool.
findings.evidence: Authentication-Results: mx.victim.com; spf=fail smtp.mailfrom=malicious-relay.top; dkim=none; dmarc=fail action=quarantine header.from=paypa1-secure.com
findings.reasoning: Authentication headers can be informative but may be forged or misinterpreted outside the receiving mail infrastructure.
findings.recommended_action: Treat header-reported auth results as hints; verify with trusted mail gateway/server-side logs when possible.
